ann.title: Reminder for ECO2021 Final Exam
ann.body:
ECO2021 final exam will take place on December 19 (Thursday), 8.30 am-10.30 am. Please keep the following in mind:
 
1. Dictionary: Each exam room will provide 1 dictionary. During busy times, borrowing will be limited to 3 minutes per use. Please do NOT bring your own dictionary, which will be considered as “other paper materials”.
 
2. Belongings: Do not forget to bring your simple calculator (non-programmable, and without the ability to store text), 2B pencil and eraser. It may be difficult to borrow them after the exam starts.
 
3. For all other requirements and instructions, please refer to the announcement from course staff on December 2.
 
Wish you all the best for the final exam!

ann.title: Final exam: sample exam, information and policies
ann.body:
Our lecture will be finished on Dec 2 (next Monday). There will be no more lectures provided by me after the day. Tutorials will continue regularly until the last teaching week. I will hold a few more office hours for the next two weeks, which will be announced later.
Under BB content, I have posted a sample final exam for you to practice. Our final exam will take place on Dec 19 (Thursday), 8:30am - 10:30am. The exam location will be arranged by the registry, to which you should follow your seat arrangements. The final exam will be a 120 minutes closed-book exam with 20 multiple choices questions and 5 free response questions. It will cover all of the topics, but with more of the weight on topics after the midterm (roughly speaking 30% before midterm and 70% after midterm). On the exam day, please arrive at least 10 minutes before the start of the exam. If you were late by more than 30 minutes, you will not be allowed to join the exam and will receive 0 points towards the midterm. Please bring to the exam your student ID and a simple calculator (non-programmable, and without the ability to store text). You may bring in other stationary (pen, ruler, eraser), but do NOT bring any paper or other materials you can write on. Scratch papers will be provided. A dictionary will be provided if you need to use it. Please bring a pencil for filling in the multiple-choice answer sheet. Furthermore, you are NOT allowed to bring books, notes, electronic devices and any means of communicating or accessing outside material. At the end of the exam, you are required to turn in all the papers, including the exam questions, answer book, multiple choice answer sheet and scratch papers. Please keep in mind that academic misconduct during examinations, verified by the Disciplinary Committee, may result in a failure grade for the course.    
For student who has a valid reason to miss the exam (getting up late or mis-remembering the exam time are not valid reasons), please contact me as early as possible to explain the situation and provide supporting documents. According to SME policy, you need to send an official application on SIS with my approval within 5 working days after the original exam. With an official approval to skip the centralized exam, you are allowed to join a make-up final exam which will be hold within 15 calendar days after centralized exam week. For detailed make-up policy, please refer to the course syllabus. If you have confusions about the exam policy, feel free to contact me or our TA.

ann.title: Midterm Exam Grade Released
ann.body:
Our midterm exam grades are posted on BB now. The average points of the three sessions that I am teaching is 69.06; median is 72; maximum is 100; and minimum is 15.
If you would like to check your exam papers, you can visit the 9th Floor of TxD on next Thursday (Nov 14) and Friday (Nov 15), 10:30am - 12:30pm and 1:30pm - 5:30pm. Our TA will be there. Each student has 5 minutes to check his/her exam papers. According to SME policies, no notes or photos are allowed to be taken. The TA will not modify the grading unless the points were added up with mistake. If you disagree with the grading, you can require the exam paper to be forwarded to me for regrade. However, please note that my regrading can possibly lead to higher or lower grades, and the updated grade will be recorded (even if it becomes lower).
For students who cannot come during the above time, you can email either one of our TAs ([person] or [person]) with a proof of time conflicts to make an appointment for another time within next week. We will NOT provide further chances to check exam papers after Nov 18.
Have a nice weekend and see you in class on Monday.

ann.title: Assignment Grading Policy and Midterm Exam of ECO2021
ann.body:
For our assignments and quizzes, I will provide a "drop-the-worst-grade" chance for each of them in the end of the semester. You don't have to apply for it. I will automatically delete the worst grade for assignments and quizzes respectively for everyone when final grades are calculated.
For our midterm exam, it will take place on Nov 3 (Sunday), 10am - 11:30am, in Liwen Hall and TA302. Another announcement will be sent later about which location you are assigned to. The midterm exam will be a 90 minutes closed-book exam with multiple choices questions and free response questions. It will cover topics 1 to 6 (Ch4 - 9) listed in the syllabus. On the exam day, please arrive at least 10 minutes before the start of the exam. If you were late by more than 30 minutes, you will not be allowed to join the exam and will receive 0 points towards the midterm. Please bring to the exam your student ID and a simple calculator (non-programmable, and without the ability to store text). You may bring in other stationary (pen, ruler, eraser), but do NOT bring any paper or other materials you can write on. Scratch papers will be provided. A dictionary will be provided if you need to use it. Please bring a pencil for filling in the multiple choice answer sheet. Furthermore, you are NOT allowed to bring books, notes, electronic devices or any means of communicating or accessing outside material. At the end of the exam, you are required to turn in all the papers, including the exam questions, answer book, multiple choice answer sheet and scratch papers. Please keep in mind that academic misconduct during examinations, verified by the Disciplinary Committee, may result in a failure grade for the course.    
For student who has a valid reason to miss the midterm exam, please contact me as early as possible to explain the situation and provide supporting documents. According to SME policy, you need to send an official applicaiton on SIS with my approval within 5 working days after the original exam. Then I will move the weight of the midterm exam to final exam. For detailed make-up policy, please refer to the course syllabus. If you have confusions about the exam and its policy, feel free to contact me or our TA.

ann.title: Lecture and Tutorial Arrangements
ann.body:
Hope you all had a smooth start during the first week of this semester. Here are several reminders and arrangements of our lectures/tutorials in the coming weeks that I would like to draw your attention:
I have updated the course syllabus on BB which now contains all information about our TA and USTF. They will start their office hours in the second week. Furthermore, I also included tentative contents for tutorials at the last page.
Quiz 2 and Assignment 1 will be posted at 12:30am on Monday (Sep 9), with deadlines on Sunday (Sep 15), 11:59pm. They will be counted in your final grades.
Our first tutorial will start in week 3 (you can check the schedules in the syllabus). However, due to the Mid-Autumn Festival, the Tuesday sessions on Sep 17 will be canceled, while the Wednesday sessions will not be affected. In order to keep all tutorial sessions consistent, I will arrange make up sessions on Sep 21 (Saturday), 1:30pm - 2:20pm (T01), 2:30pm - 3:20pm (T02), 3:30pm - 4:20pm (T03), in Teaching Complex B205. For students registed with Tuesday sessions who cannot join the make-up tutorials, you can also attend the Wednesday sessions instead for that week.
There will be a make-up lecture on Sep 14 (Saturday) in the regular lecture time and location according to the university academic calendar.
There will be no tutorials during the National Day week, so we don't need to hold any make-up tutorials on Sep 29.
Have a nice weekend and see you on Monday.
